entries.title: Line-start em-dash collapse: an autocorrected dash at line start is re-expanded to two hyphens
entries.trigger: Typing a hyphen then an em dash at the very start of a line
entries.behaviour: An input handler records the last inserted character. On a subsequent insertion with an empty selection it fires only when all three conditions hold: the previous insertion was a single hyphen; the new insertion is an em dash (the character operating-system autocorrect typically produces from a double hyphen); and the caret is at the very start of a line. It then inserts two hyphens at the caret and places the caret after them, tagged as a plain typing event. The purpose is to protect the start of a horizontal rule or a setext-heading underline from autocorrect. The handler bails out when a composition is in progress or the document is read-only (entry.js 163813-163841).
edge_cases: The rule keys off the PREVIOUS insertion, so it is stateful across two keystrokes
Only the line start is protected; a mid-line double hyphen is left to autocorrect

entries.title: NEGATIVE: pairing is not suppressed inside code spans or code blocks
entries.trigger: Typing an opening bracket or Markdown marker inside a code span or fenced code block
entries.behaviour: An explicit negative result. Searches for a suppression predicate around the pairing path returned nothing, and the close-brackets implementation installed by the editor has no verbatim gate. Pairing therefore remains active inside inline code spans and fenced code blocks. Only a small 'before' character string suppresses pairing, and it is about the preceding character, not the region: close-paren, close-bracket, close-brace, single quote, double quote, colon, semicolon and greater-than. The editor's verbatim awareness exists elsewhere — the fold service, and the region tests used by list continuation and link activation — but it is not wired into pairing.
edge_cases: This is a bounded negative over the pairing path, not a proof about every code path in the product
The absence is user-visible: typing a backtick inside an existing code span produces a pair

entries.title: NEGATIVE: there are no Markdown line-start input rules — only three bespoke typing rules exist
entries.trigger: Typing a heading, bullet, ordered marker, blockquote or task prefix at the start of a line
entries.behaviour: An explicit negative result. The extraction found exactly THREE bespoke typing rules in the whole editor: a frontmatter delimiter rule, an iOS-specific dash rule, and a CJK bracket rule. None of them is a Markdown line-start input rule. Heading, bullet, ordered, blockquote and task prefixes are therefore NOT transformed by any input rule: typing a hash then a space leaves exactly those two characters, and the rendered result comes from the Markdown parser rather than from an input rule rewriting the text. The prefixes are only RECOGNISED, by the smart-Home prefix pattern, which is a caret-motion aid rather than an input transformation. This means there is no precedence problem to solve and no undo grouping to define for these constructs, because there is nothing to undo.

edge_cases: This is a bounded negative over the editor's typing-rule registrations

entries.title: Fold markers are parsed into an attribute, and clicking the chevron only toggles DOM state
entries.trigger: Clicking the fold chevron or the title of a foldable callout
entries.behaviour: The parser captures a plus or minus immediately after the closing bracket, requiring whitespace or end-of-line after it, and stores it. The renderer writes it to a data attribute whose values are exactly '+', '-' or the empty string. The post-processor only builds fold UI when the value is '+' or '-', adding a collapsible class, creating a fold div containing a chevron icon, and toggling a collapsed class plus a slide animation on click. entries.title: Live Preview replaces the whole callout with one block widget when the selection does not touch it
entries.trigger: Moving the caret into or out of a callout in Live Preview
entries.behaviour: The callout range is detected from the syntax tree: it starts at the line carrying both the callout marker and a first-level quote marker, and extends while consecutive quote lines continue (a gap of more than one character breaks the range). When the selection does not touch that range, the range is replaced by ONE block widget carrying the rendered callout. The touch predicate is inclusive: selection.from <= rangeEnd AND selection.to >= rangeStart, so a zero-length caret anywhere inside the block counts. Selection is only considered while the editor has focus. An overlapping search-match highlight also suppresses the widget. There is no partial reveal of the marker, the fold marker or the title: the whole block is either rendered or raw (entry.js 194616-194635, 194400-194421, 194281-194284, 33682-33692, 33693-33702).

entries.title: Right-click on a callout offers a type submenu that mutates the document
entries.trigger: Right-clicking a rendered callout in Live Preview
entries.behaviour: The widget installs a contextmenu handler. The menu has an edit item that selects the widget's source range, then a submenu titled 'Callout type' with one item per menu-table key in the order info, important, tip, success, question, warning, example, quote. Each item is checked when it equals the RAW current type text (so an upper-cased marker shows nothing checked) and its click replaces ONLY the text between '[!' and ']' — the fold marker is untouched. An 'Other…' item opens a free-text picker whose items are the alias list. A 'None' item removes the callout: it deletes the whole first line including its newline and strips the quote prefix from each following line, leaving the body as plain text. All three are document mutations, unlike the fold click (entry.js 193727-193751, 193622-193638, 193639-193654, 193655-193678, 195296-195346, 33811-33824).

entries.title: Paste dispatches on a custom MIME type first, then HTML with a sentinel, then plain text
entries.trigger: Pasting into the editor
entries.behaviour: The paste path is the editor's clipboard paste hook, which delegates to a data-transfer handler. The handler recognises a Markdown MIME type, a product-specific properties MIME type, HTML, and plain text. Internal Obsidian clipboard payloads are marked in the HTML by a sentinel comment so that an in-app copy/paste round-trip is not re-converted. Plain text and a URI list are the fallbacks. HTML-to-Markdown conversion is performed by a turndown-style converter and is gated by the auto-convert setting (entry.js 165956, 115093, 114973, 94148).

entries.title: Thirteen editor commands DO ship default hotkeys, registered outside the config object
entries.trigger: A fresh install with no saved hotkey customisation
entries.behaviour: The default configuration object carries an empty hotkeys map, which an earlier reading took to mean that no editor command ships with a default binding. That is WRONG. entries.title: The reading view uses two different comment rules, inline and block, with a line-start gate

entries.behaviour: A first list of undocumented editor surfaces was compiled, including: the image resize corner and its double-click reset; the image reveal gap, spacer and tooltip; the toggle-readable-line-length and toggle-line-numbers commands; cycle-list-checklist; insert-horizontal-rule; insert-mathblock and toggle-inline-math; toggle-comments; rename-heading; add-cursor-above and add-cursor-below; swap-line-up and swap-line-down; delete-paragraph; download-attachments; toggle-keyboard; toggle-fold-properties; clear-formatting; indent-list and unindent-list; toggle-spellcheck; configure-toolbar; save-file; editor-focus; and the line-start em-dash collapse rule. Each was confirmed as a registration literal or an observed code path and then searched for across the swept pages with no hit.

states.each-item: present in the artifact, absent from the swept documentation

edge_cases: This is a bounded negative over the swept page set, not a claim about the whole documentation corpus
unknowns: The list is a first pass, not exhaustive

entries.title: The editor's default configuration is not documented, and two defaults conflict with the documentation
entries.trigger: Reading the default configuration object
entries.behaviour: Eighteen editor-relevant defaults are absent from the help pages, and two are actively misleading. The documentation for 'Indent using tabs' describes only the OFF state ('turn this off to indent using 4 spaces'), which reads as if spaces were the default; the artifact defaults the key to true, so TABS are the default indent character. The documentation for automatic link updating says to disable the setting 'if you want to be prompted instead', implying it is on by default; the artifact defaults the key to false (entry.js 94123-94206).
edge_cases: Both need runtime or vault-level corroboration before being treated as user-visible defaults

documentation.claim: Turn this off to indent using 4 spaces.

unknowns: Whether a migration path overrides alwaysUpdateLinks on upgrade
